findings.summary: A Snowmass 2021 white paper co-signed by the originators of Born geometry (Freidel, Leigh), Kowalski-Glikman and the metastring school (Berglund, Hübsch, Minic). In the setting of Born geometry and modular spacetime it states that the metaparticles are quanta of fields in the modular representation and that each observed quantum field has a 'dual' which could be associated with dark-matter degrees of freedom, citing Minic 2020 (arXiv:2003.00318) for it; it adds that dark matter, dark energy and visible matter are naturally correlated in this description.
findings.difference: It states C1's central identification, dark matter as the duals of the observed fields, but in one hedged clause that defers to Minic 2020. It does not say that the dual fields are organized in momentum space or gravitate like ours. It has no spontaneous breaking or polarization order parameter, no velocity gate and no monopoles. Its dark sector is correlated with visible matter (the MDM correlation of refs. [45, 46]), against strict P4's gravity-only coupling and permanent direct-detection null. Framework: metastring theory, intrinsically non-commutative, T-duality covariant. Workflow 1 already holds the school's fuller and earlier statements (Minic Feb 2020; Berglund-Hübsch-Minic 2020; 2202.05104) and labels them 'anticipates'. This paper's weight is that Freidel, Leigh and Kowalski-Glikman co-sign the identification. It is labeled partial here because its own statement is weaker; harmonize with workflow 1 if needed.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed as partial. Metadata: INSPIRE (recid 2032186) and the arXiv API agree on the title, the seven authors (INSPIRE and the paper spell 'Hubsch') and the year. arXiv posted it on 14 Feb 2022, one version, with the comment 'Contribution to Snowmass 2021' and no journal-ref. INSPIRE lists it as a conference paper under C21-07-11, which INSPIRE's conference record names 'Snowmass 2021' (Seattle, 17-26 July 2022). It has no DOI, and Crossref finds no journal version, so it is an arXiv preprint only. Quotes: lit.py quote finds all three verbatim in the full text (exact matches). Reading: I read the whole text (about 21k characters). The dark-matter statement is one clause in the 'Observations:' paragraph: fields in the modular representation are bi-local and non-commutative, 'and each observed quantum field has a "dual", which could be associated with dark matter degrees of freedom [11]'. Here 'dual' means the Born/T-dual partner; it is not a word collision. Reference [11] (Minic, arXiv:2003.00318) writes a dark-matter Lagrangian L~_dm(A~) for the duals A~ of the Standard Model fields on the dual coordinates x~, whose metric 'encodes ... the transverse energy-momentum space geometry'. It calls the Standard Model's dual the 'dark matter sector', in a passage on Born reciprocity between spacetime and energy-momentum space. Why not related: the paper does state C1's central identification, dark matter as the dual counterpart of each observed field, in a Born-geometry setting, so it does more than share a theme. Why not anticipates: the clause is hedged ('could be associated') and defers to [11]. The paper never says where the duals live (it uses 'momentum' only in the relative-locality paragraph), that they gravitate like ours, or how they couple. Greps find no 'spontan', 'polari', 'monopol' or 'detect', and 'gate' occurs only inside 'investigated'. Correction to the reader's difference text: the 'natural correlation' is cited to the modified-dark-matter (MDM) papers [45, 46]. In those papers the halo profile depends on the baryons through a critical acceleration set by Lambda, in a model 'inspired by gravitational thermodynamics' (1709.04388 abstract). Neither paper proposes a non-gravitational coupling between dark matter and baryons (1709.04388 full text: 0 matches for 'non-gravitational'). [46] also says its quanta's non-locality 'may explain why, so far, dark matter detection experiments have failed to detect dark matter particles'. So the correlation sets this paper apart from the program's chi, whose halos come from ordinary gravity plus the gate. But it is not evidence against strict P4's gravity-only coupling or against row 7's null, and the paper says nothing about detection. The non-gravitational coupling between visible and dual matter that workflow 1 notes comes from other papers of the school (BHM 2020 section 4; 2212.06086), not from this one. Minor: the paper has run-in headings. Quotes 1 and 3 are in 'Observations:' and quote 2 is in 'Theoretical foundations:', so the 'where' field's 'no section headings' should be fixed. Minic is also one of the originators of Born geometry (Freidel, Leigh and Minic 2014).

findings.citation: Gabriel Lopes Cardoso and Thomas Mohaupt, "Special geometry, Hessian structures and applications", Phys. Rept. 855 (2020) 1; arXiv:1909.06240 (journal; review article)
findings.summary: A review of N=2 special geometry. Its §4 reformulates point-particle Lagrangians (a theorem of Cardoso, de Wit and Mahapatra 2013, arXiv:1206.0577, not read) so that the canonical coordinates (phi^i, pi_i) are twice the real parts of a symplectic vector (x^i, F_i), and says that canonical transformations on phase space, the Sp(2n,R) maps that include (phi, pi) -> (pi, -phi), play the role electric-magnetic duality transformations play in Maxwell-type theories; invariance under them is 'often called duality invariance'. Its §5 calls the split of the special real coordinates into x^I = Re X^I and y_I = Re F_I, the electric and magnetic components, 'the choice of a polarization'. This is, in print, the formal correspondence behind #11 §11.3: Born's rho and S-duality generated by the same matrix, and a duality frame as a Lagrangian polarization.
findings.difference: The correspondence is formal: it rewrites one particle's mechanics in special-geometry language, with the phase-space variables standing in for electric and magnetic components. It assigns no physical electric or magnetic charge to the position or the momentum polarization, puts no magnetic matter in momentum space, has no vacuum that makes both choices, and holds for any symplectic pairing, which is round 2's objection ('matrix coincidence is not physical identity') rather than support for the conjecture's physics. Useful as a checked source for the [T] half of #11 §11.3, which cites 17-dagger for the polarization language.

Leads outside C2-C4, not findings: Smolin 2015 (arXiv:1503.01424) obtains Born duality X -> P, P -> -X as a remnant of an SO(1,2) symmetry of a cubic matrix model and says relativistic particles and strings follow from 'breaking that basic triality ... to a duality' by choice of compactification (quotes checked FOUND), which bears on the program's hard core (broken reciprocity), not on C1-C7; Kupriyanov, Sharapov and Szabo 2023 (arXiv:2308.07406) build Born reciprocity into symplectic groupoids and obtain a compact momentum space S^3 ('a remarkable duality between the noncommutativity of spacetime and the curvature of momentum space', FOUND), which bears on the closed-universe note's compact momentum space; Alfonsi's thesis (arXiv:2108.10297, PDF) says 'The choice of polarisation in quantisation then becomes the choice of duality frame' for T-duality in DFT, a parallel to P5's polarization language that FLM already have. The nonassociative R-flux line (Bakas-Lust, Lust-Malek-Szabo, Szabo) and Harvey-Jensen's KK monopole localized in winding space, which some listed papers cite, were assessed by workflow 1 (g2, g3) and are not repeated.

The paper ties the growth of a_I toward the Big Bang to 'a dominance of the dark energy' there. It obtains today's acceleration from a dark-energy density Λ a_R^{3(β−1)}, which for β = 1 is a cosmological constant.

The shrinking partner a_I is not the source of the late acceleration, which comes from the dark-energy density Λ a_R^{3(β−1)} (constant for β = 1), and its influence runs the other way: large a_I goes with dark-energy dominance near the Big Bang. Its law is a_I ∝ a_R⁻⁴, not a·ã = 1, and there is no conjugate matter, no collapse and no w_eff = −w̃. The pseudo-imaginary part is velocity space in Caianiello's sense, not a spontaneously selected polarization.
